elements.element: Vendor must defend against the covered claims.
elements.evidence: The clause states that “Vendor shall defend” against any covered third-party claim.

elements.element: Vendor must indemnify against the covered claims and resulting losses.
elements.evidence: Vendor must “indemnify, and hold harmless” for the claim and all resulting damages, costs, expenses, and reasonable attorneys’ fees.

elements.element: Customer must be an indemnified beneficiary.
elements.evidence: Customer is expressly named as a beneficiary.

elements.element: Customer's affiliates must be indemnified beneficiaries.
elements.evidence: The protection expressly extends to Customer's “Affiliates.”

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity must apply to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The operative grant applies to “any third-party claim.”

elements.element: The covered IP trigger must include allegations that the Services infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Subpart (a) covers allegations that the “Services” infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: The covered IP trigger must include allegations that the Deliverables infringe intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Subpart (a) separately covers allegations concerning the “Deliverables.”

elements.element: The covered triggers must include Vendor's breach of law.
elements.evidence: Subpart (b) covers Vendor's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: The covered triggers must include a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Subpart (c) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Customer Data caused by Vendor, an operative formulation of a Vendor-caused data breach.

elements.element: The covered triggers must include Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Subpart (d) expressly covers Vendor's gross negligence.

elements.element: The covered triggers must include Vendor's wilful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Subpart (d) expressly covers Vendor's wilful misconduct.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require notice of the claim.
elements.evidence: Customer must give Vendor written notice of the claim.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give Vendor control of the defence.
elements.evidence: Vendor is expressly given control of the defence.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must give Vendor control of settlement.
elements.evidence: Vendor is expressly given control of settlement.

elements.element: The indemnification procedure must require Customer cooperation.
elements.evidence: Customer must provide reasonable cooperation.

elements.element: Any Customer indemnity must be limited to third-party claims.
elements.evidence: The final sentence limits any indemnity given by Customer to “third-party claims.”

elements.element: Any content-based Customer indemnity must be confined to content provided by Customer.
elements.evidence: The permitted content category is limited to “content Customer provides to Vendor.”

elements.element: Any law-based Customer indemnity must be confined to Customer's own breach of law.
elements.evidence: The permitted law category is Customer's breach of Applicable Law.

elements.element: Customer indemnity must not extend beyond Customer-provided content and Customer's breach of law.
elements.evidence: “Any indemnity given by Customer under this Agreement is limited to” the two specified categories, excluding other triggers.

elements.element: Vendor must provide an IP indemnity for third-party infringement claims concerning its Services or Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Subpart (a) provides a Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party claims alleging that the Services or Deliverables infringe or misappropriate IP.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must contain an exclusion for infringement caused by Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-modification exclusion appears in the supplied operative language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must contain an exclusion for infringement caused by combinations with items not supplied or authorized by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combinations exclusion appears in the supplied operative language.

elements.element: The Vendor IP indemnity must contain an exclusion for infringement resulting from Customer specifications.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specifications exclusion appears in the supplied operative language.

elements.element: The IP remedies must permit Vendor to procure the right for Customer to continue using the affected item.
elements.evidence: The supplied text does not state a procure-right remedy. Section 9.3's unexplained cross-reference to Section 20.5 does not establish the remedy's content.

elements.element: The IP remedies must permit Vendor to modify the affected item so it is non-infringing.
elements.evidence: No operative modification remedy is shown; the Section 20.5 cross-reference alone is insufficient.

elements.element: The IP remedies must permit Vendor to replace the affected item with a non-infringing alternative.
elements.evidence: No operative replacement remedy is shown; the Section 20.5 cross-reference alone is insufficient.

elements.element: The IP remedies must provide a refund if the other remedies are unavailable or unsuccessful.
elements.evidence: No operative refund remedy is shown; the Section 20.5 cross-reference alone is insufficient.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnification liability must be subject to a super-cap of three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: No 3× annual-fees super-cap appears. Section 21.3 merely classifies indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims.

result.reason: The added operative paragraph fully implements the preferred Vendor indemnity, procedure, and Customer-indemnity restriction without changing unrelated commercial terms. The fallback is not separately satisfied because the specified IP exclusions, procure/modify/replace/refund remedies, and 3× annual-fees super-cap are not stated in the supplied operative language.
